why: Check 1's conditions stay within its expect line. PASS needs the run to print `{}`, give `exit=0` and show no SyntaxError trace, with loadConfig in src/config.js doing the parse and the catch. The stderr warning and the missing-file behaviour are correctly listed under Advisory. Check 2 breaks the criterion. The words "npm test passes" only require the tests to pass with a zero exit code. But PASS also requires "the output shows `# fail 0`", and FAIL triggers when "the output shows `# fail` greater than 0". That makes an exact line of test-runner (TAP) output part of the PASS condition. If npm test passed with a reporter that doesn't print that line, the check could not pass. That exact-wording test belongs under Advisory, not in PASS or FAIL.
